clue.text: Not diluted, we hear, by this bit of water

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the spelling may differ from the sound

blocks.note: a drink taken straight is not diluted with water or mixer

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of drinking their spirit neat, beside a stretch of sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel of sea joining two larger bodies of water, such as Dover's.

clue.text: Share tipping system

blocks.note: surface reading: a stock-market tip about which shares to buy
setter's reading: a scheme by which restaurant tips are pooled and shared among the staff

explanation.walkthrough: Share tipping sounds like the City pundit's trade; read it instead as tips being shared out among waiters and kitchen staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A tronc is the pool into which a restaurant's gratuities are put, then divided among employees by an agreed scheme.

clue.text: Speaker interred in NE Corunna

indicators.note: something buried is hidden and mixed in with the soil, so the letters lie jumbled inside the place name

blocks.note: the compass abbreviation and the Spanish port, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A speaker has been laid to rest in the north-east of the Spanish city of Corunna.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcer is someone who speaks on air, introducing programmes or reading news, so a broadcast speaker.

clue.text: Goes up in smoke at last, like Melpomene

indicators.note: the last of the word at is the only letter kept from it
in a down clue going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: the final letter of at
a cigar is something you smoke

explanation.surface: Something goes up in smoke at last, a fate fit for a tragic heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed smoke sits after the last letter of at. Melpomene is the Greek Muse of tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Melpomene was the Muse of tragedy, so anything resembling her is tragic in character.

clue.text: Member of sect to cite as evidence in Kent, perhaps

indicators.note: one word sits inside another, with the region wrapped round it

blocks.note: Kent is an example of a county in the South East of England
to adduce something is to cite it as evidence

explanation.surface: A religious sect member is cited in evidence somewhere in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Perhaps marks Kent as one example of the South East, written SE; the verb sits between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sadducees were a Jewish party of priests and aristocrats in the time of Jesus, rivals of the Pharisees.

clue.text: Long room where pictures are executed?

definitions.text: Long room where pictures are executed?

blocks.clueFragment: Long room where pictures are executed?
blocks.note: surface reading: an art gallery's long room where paintings are made
setter's reading: executed as in killed, so the targets in a long room are shot

explanation.walkthrough: Pictures are executed sounds like artists at work; the question mark lets execute mean kill, so the pictures are targets being shot at.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting gallery is a long indoor range where people fire at targets, often painted figures, for practice or fun.

clue.text: Up when due in, and seen to go off

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: ETA, estimated time of arrival, says when a train or plane is due in
something noted has been seen

explanation.surface: An arrival time is posted and then seen to go off, like a delayed train board.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate is to explode, and a bomb that goes off has exploded.

clue.text: Dark - can't be a foreign wagon

blocks.note: first meaning: without light
second meaning, whimsical: un- means not, and a lit is the French sleeper of wagon-lit, so the word reads as not a sleeper car

explanation.walkthrough: A wagon-lit is a sleeping car on a continental train; the setter splits the answer as un-lit, something that is not a lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A room with no lamp or fire burning is in darkness, the plain everyday adjective for no light.

clue.text: Dame Ellen changed and put.on a shiny coat

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters of the name are rearranged

blocks.note: the title and first name taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An actress, Dame Ellen, changes costume and puts on a glossy coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stop between put and on is a printing slip in the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy coating, so an object enamelled has been given a hard shiny finish.

clue.text: It may be a fair ride to the junction

blocks.clueFragment: It may be a fair ride
blocks.note: first meaning: a merry-go-round at a funfair
second meaning: a circular road junction with traffic going round an island

explanation.surface: It's only a short, fair journey to the road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair ride sounds like a reasonable distance; fair is the funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a funfair carousel and a circular traffic intersection, common in Britain.

clue.text: Conductor -or first player?

blocks.note: first meaning: an electrical wire or cable
second meaning: the person who plays first at cards, or the principal performer

explanation.walkthrough: Conductor suggests an orchestra; here it is the electric cable.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical flex is a lead, and at bridge the player who starts a trick has the lead.

clue.text: Inform of unusual addition to the bill

indicators.note: an addition to something is tacked on after it, so one word follows the other

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
quaint means oddly old-fashioned, unusual

explanation.surface: A diner is told of an odd extra item on the restaurant bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone with a fact is to make them aware of it, to inform them.

clue.text: Grumble when knave deserts croaker

indicators.note: whatever deserts leaves the scene, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: the natterjack is a British toad, famous for its loud croak
the knave in a pack of cards is also called the jack

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles when the rogue walks out on an old moaner.
explanation.walkthrough: Croaker suggests a gloomy complainer; it is the natterjack toad.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chatter at length, and in older or regional use to nag or grumble.

clue.text: Brandy to take back to study

indicators.note: taking something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to cram is to study hard before an exam

explanation.surface: A student takes the brandy back to their room to study.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a spirit distilled from the skins and pips left after grapes are pressed for wine.

clue.text: Carrier that ran for 17's second half

definitions.text: Carrier that ran for 17's second half

blocks.note: surface reading: a cart or wagon that ran along the road
setter's reading: a play that ran in the theatre for the author named by the back half of 17 down, Shaw

explanation.walkthrough: The second half of 17 down is SHAW, and his 1929 play The Apple Cart had a long run; the carrier is the cart in its title.
explanation.definitionFit: An applecart is a barrow for fruit, and The Apple Cart is George Bernard Shaw's political comedy.

clue.text: Receptacle for essence

blocks.note: first meaning: the hard case that holds a kernel
second meaning: as in the phrase in a ..., meaning in essence

explanation.surface: A container made to hold perfume essence.
explanation.walkthrough: Essence suggests a scent bottle; it is the idiom in a nutshell, meaning briefly, in essence.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard case round a kernel holds it, and to put something in a nutshell is to give its essence.

clue.text: Goodfellow, though an ugly little devil

blocks.note: first meaning: Robin Goodfellow, the mischievous sprite also called Puck
second meaning: a small grotesque goblin or imp

explanation.surface: He's a good fellow, even if he is an ugly little so-and-so.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Goodfellow is Puck of English folklore and A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck, Robin Goodfellow, is the traditional English sprite of that kind, and the word also means any mischievous imp.

clue.text: Thrill over Corno di Bassetto - what delicacy!

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the first word sits on top of the second

blocks.note: a kick is a thrill, as in doing it for kicks
Corno di Bassetto was the pen-name George Bernard Shaw used as a music critic

explanation.surface: Someone thrills to an Italian horn player and exclaims at how exquisite the playing is.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian name looks like a musician or an instrument (it is a basset horn), but it is Shaw in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickshaw is a fancy little dish or trifle, from French quelque chose, so a dainty delicacy.

clue.text: Is this partner a Wrangler?

blocks.note: surface reading: a Cambridge Wrangler, a top mathematics graduate, or a cowboy handling horses
setter's reading: the partner a boxer trains with is one who sparrs, and to spar is also to wrangle or argue

explanation.walkthrough: Wrangler, capitalised, looks like the Cambridge title; lower-case it is just someone who argues, as a boxer's practice partner spars.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparring partner trains a boxer with practice bouts, and the phrase also means someone you regularly argue with.

clue.text: Waited to be an omen

blocks.note: first meaning: the old past tense of bide, to wait
second meaning: to portend

explanation.walkthrough: The verb bide, to wait, has an archaic past tense the same as this four-letter word for foreshadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Bide means wait and its old past tense is bode, while to bode is also to signal what will come.

clue.text: Coach party full of Wales, by the sound of it

blocks.note: first meaning: to train or teach
second meaning: a group of whales, with Wales standing in for its sound-alike

explanation.surface: A coach party packed with Welsh travellers, judging by the noise they make.
explanation.walkthrough: A coach party sounds like a bus trip from Wales; by the sound of it says Wales stands for whales, and a group of whales is a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train them, and a group of whales, dolphins or fish swimming together is a school.

clue.text: Exist with four full suits for ornament

indicators.note: one thing with another stands next to it, so the two words run on

blocks.note: to be is to exist
a complete pack of playing cards holds all four suits

explanation.surface: Getting by with four smart suits to dress up in.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedeck is to adorn or decorate, which is what the verb ornament means.

clue.text: Lifting this could almost produce a wobble - for its owner?

definitions.text: Lifting this could almost produce a wobble - for its owner?

blocks.clueFragment: Lifting this could almost produce a wobble
blocks.note: letter play: in a down light, the answer read upwards is one letter short of wobble

blocks.clueFragment: Lifting this could almost produce a wobble - for its owner?
blocks.note: setter's reading: raising this joint to drink too often makes the drinker unsteady

explanation.walkthrough: Elbow-lifting is slang for heavy drinking, which makes a person wobble; the five letters written upwards also read WOBLE, almost wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the arm joint bent when raising a glass, hence the idiom for drinking a lot.

clue.text: Lose cars, perhaps, in this rackety game

indicators.note: perhaps says the words are only one possible arrangement, so the letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: In a noisy, rough game you might well lose your cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Rackety looks like noisy; it means played with rackets, the netted sticks of this sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is played with a long stick carrying a net, a kind of racket, so it is a racket game.

clue.text: Half sure what Munnings was previously

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, its back half dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
Sir Alfred Munnings, painter of horses, was President of the Royal Academy, PRA

explanation.surface: Someone is half certain what the painter Munnings did before he was famous.
explanation.walkthrough: Munnings was PRA from 1944 to 1949; supra is Latin, used in texts to refer to something above or earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Supra, Latin for above, is used in writing to mean earlier in the text, previously mentioned.

clue.text: Palace with no room for the poor young innocent

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the little word appears in scrambled form
leaving no room for something means it is shut out and taken away

blocks.note: Lambeth Palace is the London home of the Archbishop of Canterbury
taken as written, then scrambled and removed

explanation.surface: A palace has no room for the poor, an innocent child is turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: The poor looks like the needy; poor scrambles the, and that scrambled word is dropped from the end of the palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb is a young sheep, and the word is used for any meek, innocent person, especially a child.

clue.text: Name dropper, highly prone to be made into a symbol

indicators.note: a dropper lets something fall, so the name's letter is let go
being made into something new means the letters are refashioned in another order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A social-climbing name dropper, given to it, is made into a symbol of snobbery.
explanation.walkthrough: Name dropper looks like a snob; it means drop the N of name from the letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hieroglyph is a picture character in Egyptian writing, a symbol standing for a word or sound.

clue.text: Pack off free-tripper

blocks.note: first meaning: to ..., put things away
second meaning: someone who travels hidden aboard without paying

explanation.walkthrough: Pack off reads as send away; it is to stow away, pack things off out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow away is to pack things into storage, and a stowaway sails or flies hidden, travelling free.

clue.text: Carrier opening in mid-April and August

indicators.note: the word opens up in the middle of the phrase, running across the gap between words

blocks.note: the end of the spring month, the joining word and the start of the summer month

explanation.surface: A shipping carrier starts service between April and August.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening also fits the answer, a carriage whose hood folds back.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top, a vehicle carrying passengers.
